reason: The core defect is verified in source and in the browser, but two thirds of the proposed fix are wrong and one third would break a green gate. Driving ?v=approach&state=day at 390x844: .b-item count is 0, .b-behindRow count is 9 and offsetParent-visible count is 0, because render-b.js behindBlock() does render every past row and b.css:290 kills them with [data-past="folded"] .b-behindRow { display: none }. So on the wedding morning the artifact holds the nine milestones in the DOM and shows the reader none of them, and the approach room offers no way to ask for them -- the only 'ask' that exists is the console's past=folded|listed room switch (render-core.js:250), which is a lab control the guest does not have. lock.md's rule is 'stated in a sentence, listed in full only if asked for'; a closed-by-default disclosure IS that rule, made available to the person it was written for, so it does not reopen the lock, it completes the half of it that was never built. It also rescues the round-1 remediation the fold silently defeated: the confirmed sharpened fix on the-day-has-no-day-in-it asked for behindBlock at the day-of clock precisely because 'that is the keepsake reading', and folded, it reads as nothing. The closing-order claim is exact: behindBlock's note at clock 2026-10-03 renders 'Venue walk-through, 19 September. The city hotel shortlist is not going ahead.', so the last content sentence a guest reads on the morning is a cancellation, with only the footer chrome after it. Where the finding is loose, and the fix must not be driven by it: the text measurements are wrong in absolute terms (innerText is 277 chars on day against 614 on desk, not 331 against 652 -- the ratio claim survives, the numbers do not), and the 'one fact five times' count is inflated. 'Mara & Finn' is not that fact and 'Saturday 3 October 2026' is the only place the date is stated. The verified duplication is smaller: 'Wedding day' renders twice (the .b-sub subtitle and .b-dayNowTitle) and the it-is-now fact three times (TODAY / 'This is the day the plan was for.' / HAPPENING NOW). Two elements of the fix are refused outright. (1) 'render a Where to be line from F.project.primaryDate.label plus the venue' is already built and already asserted -- it is the .b-sub line 'Wedding day at The Orchard' added by the round-1 fix, and interaction-check.mjs:708 asserts it. The finding lists that exact string among its redundancies and then proposes adding it back, which is self-cancelling. (2) 'delete the Happening now section' would break interaction-check.mjs:709, 'the day names what is happening' (/happening now/i && /wedding day/i), an assertion written to close the confirmed round-1 finding that this screen denied its own live milestone; deleting b-dayNote as well would strip the one line of feeling from the surface the brief calls the one with the most feeling in it, and trade round 1's fix for round 2's. And 'render the folded milestones as the same .b-item rows desk and phone use' aims at the wrong element: .b-item is positioned by away x pixels-per-day on the measure, every past item is negative at the day-of clock, and reusing it would either stack rows off the origin or force new machinery for rows that already exist as .b-behindRow. Confirmed on the hole, sharpened on everything else.
sharpenedFix: Do not delete the day's copy and do not touch .b-item. Fix the one thing that is actually missing -- the ask -- and fix it where the hole is, in behindBlock(). In render-b.js behindBlock(), wrap the past rows in a native <details> whose <summary> is the existing h2.b-behindLabel text plus a count drawn from the same accessor ('Behind you -- 9 things', done.length + dropped.length, no hand arithmetic), leaving h2.b-behindLabel as the summary's own content so the region keeps its heading. Order inside: summary, then the rows, then the b-behindNote sentence LAST, so the cancellation is never what a reader lands on before the footer -- that alone fixes the closing-order half of the finding and costs one line move. Gate it on the density decision rather than on the state: under [data-past="folded"] the details is closed by default and b.css:290 becomes redundant (delete it -- do not keep a display:none fighting a disclosure); under [data-past="listed"] force it open (details[open] plus summary { display: none } or the open attribute set at render time) so the record room and print are unchanged and the print sheet never prints a collapsed control. This is one change in one function and it closes the same hole on phone, desk and day at once, rather than inventing a component that exists on one state. Keep .b-sub, keep b-dayNote, keep the Happening now section -- three green assertions depend on the first two of those and the third is the round-1 remediation. If the panel wants the 'Wedding day' duplication gone, the correct edit is inside the section, not the section itself: render h2.b-behindLabel 'Happening now' with the milestone's own date line rather than repeating the title that already sits in the subtitle two lines above, or drop .b-dayNowTitle and let the label sit under the subtitle. Verify the summary against the audit gate's hit-target and radii rules (a summary is a control; it needs the 44px target and the declared radius set), give it no transition beyond the declared 0.14s easing family, and confirm the disclosure marker is drawn in fore-ladder ink, not a fourth hue or a UA triangle. Then extend interaction-check.mjs: the day state renders zero visible .b-behindRow closed and exactly behind(dayClock).length open; the summary is keyboard-operable and its expanded state is exposed; the b-behindNote sentence follows the rows in DOM order on every state that renders behindBlock; print renders the rows expanded. Reshoot day, phone, desk and print at 390/768/1280/1440 in both rooms.
